explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but the text puts Jesus somewhere else. Luke 3:21 says heaven was opened "as He was praying," not while He was teaching. Nobody gets a sermon in this scene. Jesus is baptized, He prays, and then heaven opens.
You caught it, friend. Luke 3:21 says heaven was opened "as He was praying." It doesn't say a word about teaching. Jesus is baptized, He prays, and heaven opens right over that moment of prayer.
That's the one, friend. Luke 3:22 says "the Holy Spirit descended on Him." Heaven opens, and the Spirit comes down right on Jesus. Nobody has to guess who it is, because the text says it plainly.

I get why you'd pick it, since angels turn up all over Luke. I know, because one showed up in my drawer once and I'm STILL not over it. But in this scene Luke 3:22 says it's the Holy Spirit who descends on Jesus. No angel is named here.

Elijah, the prophet who spoke for God in Israel's old days, is a big name, friend, but he isn't in this scene. Luke 3:22 says "the Holy Spirit descended on Him." The Spirit comes down on Jesus, and Elijah never shows up.

Yes, friend! Luke 3:22 says the Holy Spirit descended on Him "in a bodily form like a dove." Notice the words "like a dove." That's how the text puts it, so I keep it just that way. And you know I'm happy about it, because a dove is one of my cookie cutter kids' shapes, Minty.
Flame is a fair guess, friend, since fire comes up around the Spirit elsewhere in the Bible. But here Luke 3:22 says "like a dove." That's the picture this passage gives. No flame in this scene.

A cloud makes sense, because clouds show up around God in other places in the Bible. Not this time, though. Luke 3:22 says the Spirit came down "in a bodily form like a dove." Think wings, friend, not weather.
That's it, friend. The voice says, "You are My beloved Son…" (Luke 3:22). It speaks right to Jesus, and it says Son, not anything smaller. Read that line slowly and let it sit a second.
Servant is a good word, friend, and the Bible uses it in other places. But the voice in Luke 3:22 says, "You are My beloved Son." That's the name it gives Jesus here. Son, plain and clear.

Prophet is a real title in the Bible, friend, but it's not what the voice says here. In Luke 3:22 the voice from heaven says, "You are My beloved Son…" It speaks straight to Jesus. Son is the word it uses.
Right, friend. The voice finishes with "…in You I am well pleased." (Luke 3:22) It says that straight to Jesus. Beloved Son and well pleased, both in the same breath.

Not quite, friend. The voice does say it, and the text is right there in Luke 3:22: "You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased." So the voice says Son and says well pleased, both to Jesus. I'd keep that second half close.
Yes, friend! Luke 3:23 says Jesus was "about thirty years old when He began His ministry." Notice the word "about." Luke doesn't say exactly thirty, so I don't either.
Twenty is a little young, friend. Luke 3:23 says Jesus was "about thirty years old when He began His ministry." So the number is thirty, with an "about" attached. That's all the text gives us.

Forty is a little high, friend. Luke 3:23 says Jesus was "about thirty years old when He began His ministry." Thirty is the number the text gives. I'd say forty is trying to get a promotion it didn't earn.
